method: Human runs the stand-alone KiCad PCB Calculator, TransLine tab, line type "Stripline", Analyze direction. Plane-to-plane spacing b = 1.6 mm, strip CENTRED between the planes (for T = 0.035 mm the distance from each plane to the nearest strip face is the same). The tool's substrate-height field must be the plane-to-plane spacing: confirm from its drawing, write the field names you used and how the strip position is set in this field; if the tool's height field or strip-position field means anything else, STOP and leave the case null (do not convert by hand). Record the exact KiCad version (Help > About), OS, displayed digits, the thickness model the tool names and every non-default setting. Outputs to copy: Z0_ohm = characteristic impedance shown; eps_eff = effective permittivity shown, only if the tool displays one for the stripline (else leave null). Every toolOutputs value stays null until a human copies it from a real run of the tool (all displayed digits, no rounding, no conversion). Quasi-static comparison: frequency 1 MHz (1e6 Hz) in the tool; if it refuses, use the lowest accepted frequency and write it here. Dielectric loss tangent, conductor resistivity and roughness do not affect Z0 or eps_eff in the quasi-static model: leave them at the tool defaults and record the defaults here. Dispersion: check the tool's settings, turn dispersion off if it can be turned off, otherwise record that it is on. Soldermask or cover/top-dielectric correction: disable it (or leave the top height at its no-cover default) and record the setting. Thickness: the t0 cases need T = 0 in the tool (if refused, enter the smallest accepted value and record it); the t35um cases need T = 0.035 mm; one tool run with T = 0.035 mm feeds the three t35um cases of the same geometry (none, A, B): copy the same displayed numbers into all three. Record the tool's exact name for its thickness and dispersion models. Details, field entries per case and the digits check: docs/validation/crosscheck-impedance.md. Agreement never verifies a ledger row; no third-party source is copied.

compare.why: Z0, stripline (strip centred). Derived before any run: 0.07 % prefactor (eta0/4 = 94.18 ohm against 30 pi = 94.25 ohm) + 0.10 % between the 30 pi and 94.15 constants of Steer and Rogers (ledger S-021a) + 0.50 % largest model spread recorded in S-021a (narrow-strip models and the parenthesization question: 71.20 against 70.81 ohm) + 0.10 % display rounding = 0.77 %, set to 1 %. The tool's stripline model origin is not established (research note C-K11), so a larger difference is first checked against the tool's strip-position and spacing definitions. Display-rounding term assumes the tool shows at least 2 decimals for ohm values and at least 3 decimals for eps_eff; the worksheet (section 3) requires the human to check the shown digits and re-derive this tolerance BEFORE the first run if fewer are shown.

eps_eff for a stripline: our value equals er (homogeneous dielectric, TEM; ledger S-021). Only display rounding is expected (0.0005 on a value of at least 3.5 is 0.015 %); 0.1 % is set. A larger difference means the tool reports something other than er (for example a different definition) and must be explained, not tolerated. Compare only if the tool displays it.

Z0, control case: our zero-thickness stripline against a tool run WITH strip thickness 35 um. Same 1 % tolerance as the zero-thickness comparison (derivation there). Expected to fall outside it if the tool applies a thickness correction (the miss is the tool's thickness effect, classified E3 / S-021a, not a bug); should pass if the tool ignores T. Display-rounding term assumes the tool shows at least 2 decimals for ohm values and at least 3 decimals for eps_eff; the worksheet (section 3) requires the human to check the shown digits and re-derive this tolerance BEFORE the first run if fewer are shown.

Z0, stripline with finite thickness 35 um: our opt-in wide-strip variant (ledger S-021a CONFLICT: Steer and Rogers constants differ by 0.10 %, accuracy "questionable" for thick narrow strips) against the tool's own thickness handling, whose model name the human records. Derived before any run: the 0.77 % zero-thickness derivation (see the zero-thickness cases) + 0.5 % for the undocumented difference between thickness procedures = 1.27 %, set to 1.5 %. A larger difference is a model-difference item (S-021a), not a bug, once the tool's model is recorded. Display-rounding term assumes the tool shows at least 2 decimals for ohm values and at least 3 decimals for eps_eff; the worksheet (section 3) requires the human to check the shown digits and re-derive this tolerance BEFORE the first run if fewer are shown.
